upstream_facts.brief_statement: The paper and the experiment loop patch [-1] (tasks/dist.py:312). The helper default and the notebook patch [-1, -4, -6, -8] (tasks/dist.py:200, commit c53372c).
upstream_facts.finding: get_dist fixes token_positions = [-1] (tasks/dist.py:312) and passes it to run_with_cf_hf (tasks/dist.py:353-355). The helper run_with_cf_hf uses [-1, -4, -6, -8] only when called without token_positions (tasks/dist.py:198-200); commit c53372c changed that default from [-1] and made the same change in the notebook (example.ipynb:208). The paper states that interventions patch the last-token residual stream vector (Sec. 3 introduction and Sec. 3.3). The patched tensor is the input of decoder block layer_idx, i.e. Hugging Face hidden_states[layer_idx] (tasks/dist.py:221).
paper_evidence: Sec. 3 (introduction) and Sec. 3.3: interventions on the full last-token residual stream vector at layer l

upstream_facts.brief_statement: The default readout scores only in-context entity tokens (tasks/dist.py:358), and generation is off by default.
upstream_facts.finding: The readout takes last-position logits at the token ids of the n in-context entity tokens found by the schema matcher (tasks/dist.py:328-329, 358) and stores these raw logits, not probabilities (tasks/dist.py:393); the prediction is their argmax (tasks/dist.py:360, 366-367). Generation is off by default in the command-line entry point (tasks/dist.py:424) and in the notebook (example.ipynb:100). Qualification: the function get_dist itself defaults to generate=True (tasks/dist.py:288); the command line overrides it. Entities must be single tokens (tasks/dist.py:271-273). The softmax over the n entity indices is applied later, in the paper's averaging (Sec. 4), not in tasks/dist.py.

code_evidence.text: values = logits[0, -1, [to_single_token(tokenizer, prompt_str_tokenized[i]) for i in answer_indices]]

paper_evidence: Sec. 4, 'Learning how the mechanisms are mixed': logit distributions per index combination, softmax over entity-group indices, then the mean

upstream_facts.brief_statement: It is ordered (tasks/dist.py:369-375): the first matching label wins. Never use this classification; report ties as equivalence.
upstream_facts.finding: The patch-effect label is assigned by an if/elif chain in the order positional, keyload (lexical), payload (reflexive), no_effect, else unknown (tasks/dist.py:369-378); the notebook uses the same order with labels positional, lexical, reflexive, no_effect, mixed (example.ipynb:263-271). When two candidates predict the same entity, the earlier label wins. The argmax itself breaks ties towards the lowest index (tasks/dist.py:360). This application does not use this classification.

upstream_facts.brief_statement: Upstream draws the lexical and reflexive indices independently, so they can collide. Always check admissibility on design indices.
upstream_facts.finding: In the main template (messiness 0, tasks/dist.py:487-488; used by the notebook, example.ipynb:136) the positional index is cf_query_index (training.py:1226, 1269), the reflexive index is swap_index (training.py:1236, 1240, 1263) and the lexical index is swappy_index (training.py:1249, 1265). swap_index and swappy_index are drawn independently from the same set, all indices except the recipient and donor query indices, so they coincide with probability 1/(n-2). Upstream then locates the lexical and reflexive indices by substring matching of token strings (tasks/dist.py:331-335), so a collision yields equal indices. Nothing upstream keeps the lexical, reflexive or native index away from the positional window.
paper_evidence: Sec. 3.2: i_P, i_L and i_R vary freely from 1 to n

upstream_facts.brief_statement: do_filter is off by default, so upstream does not filter cases for native correctness.
upstream_facts.finding: The command-line flag --do-filter defaults to False (tasks/dist.py:435) and is passed through (tasks/dist.py:515); with do_filter False, get_counterfactual_datasets returns unfiltered samples (training.py:376). The notebook sets do_filter=False (example.ipynb:146). Qualification: get_counterfactual_datasets itself defaults to do_filter=True (training.py:308); both entry points override it.

upstream_facts.brief_statement: The paper's App. D.1 aligns only two mechanisms: positional with reflexive at t_entity = 1, and positional with lexical at t_entity = 3. There is no three-way agreement condition.
upstream_facts.status: verified for the paper; qualified by the blog post
upstream_facts.finding: App. D.1 and the Figure 18 caption describe exactly two alignment experiments on the music task: positional with reflexive at t_entity = 1 and positional with lexical at t_entity = 3. The paper has no three-way agreement experiment, and the released template (training.py:1226-1269) cannot produce i_L = i_P or i_R = i_P. However, the blog post's Figure 1 caption shows token probabilities with all three mechanisms pointing to the same entity, and its interactive figure loads one mean probability vector for every (i_P, i_L, i_R) combination, including coinciding ones (see blog.interactive_figure). How those coinciding cells were constructed is not documented in the paper or in the released code. The Round 1 agreement control therefore remains this application's own construction, but public text must not call three-way agreement unprecedented.
paper_evidence: Sec. 4: 150 interventions per combination of 1 <= i_P, i_L, i_R <= n, stated as n^3 = 8,000 distributions

upstream_facts.brief_statement: Round 1 uses the paper's layer l.
upstream_facts.status: not stated numerically in the paper text; inferred, with an upstream inconsistency
upstream_facts.finding: The paper defines l as the last layer before retrieval (Sec. 3.3, App. D.2) without printing its value for gemma-2-2b-it. The Figure 2 caption shows layer 18 and says layers 16-18 carry binding information; the blog post says layers 19-25 already carry the retrieved entity. The notebook uses layer = 18 (example.ipynb:98); the command-line default is 17 (tasks/dist.py:415). In the upstream hook convention layer 18 means the input of decoder block 18, hidden_states[18] (tasks/dist.py:221). The value is proposed, not fixed, in PREFLIGHT_PLAN.md.

upstream_facts.brief_statement: (not in the brief) The task registry.
upstream_facts.finding: tasks/dist.py lists 14 schema constants (tasks/dist.py:88-103) and imports them at module level (tasks/dist.py:43-58), but grammar/schemas.py at c53372c defines only 10 (commit 15c1a4c removed the others). Importing SCHEMA_COLORED_SHAPES from grammar.schemas raises ImportError (checked with the standard library only), so tasks/dist.py, and the notebook's import from it, cannot be imported unmodified at this commit. The ten defined schemas match the paper's ten tasks (App. A.1, Table 1). This application does not import tasks/dist.py; its adapter reads grammar/schemas.py only.

found: Sec. 4 averages 150 interventions per (i_P, i_L, i_R) cell after a softmax over the entity indices and fits the mixture model to these means.
Mean logit or probability distributions per cell or per index (Figures 3 right, 13, 24-26; blog Figures 4, 5 and the interactive figure).

Case-level argmax labels aggregated into shares per positional (or other single) index, pooling over the other indices (Figures 2, 8-12, 14-17, 20, 21, 27, 28, 30), and confusion matrices of predicted versus positional index (Figures 3 left, 29, 31). These are descriptive shares, not per full cell, and do not compare single cases with the cell average.
